title: Keel's Solana risk budget is a quarter of its Ethereum budget, scaling exposure to distance from the home chain
content:
Comparing A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.1.1.3.1 (Ethereum) with …3.2 (Solana), Keel runs two different risk regimes. Ethereum limits cluster at `maxAmount` 100,000,000 with a 50,000,000/day slope — the USDS/USDC swap, the sUSDS deposit, the SkyLink bridge to Solana, and the CCTP USDC limits. Nearly every Solana limit is 25,000,000 with a 10,000,000/day slope: the USDS, USDC, USDT, USDG and PYUSD Reserves, each swap pair, and the bridges back to Ethereum.

The asymmetry is directional as well as absolute. Up to 100M USDS may be sent from Ethereum to Solana, but only 25M may be sent back per the Solana-side limit — so the constraint that binds is not how much can leave home, but how much can be recalled at once. Capital can be committed to the frontier faster than it can be retrieved.

Read against the previous claim, this qualifies the "unwinding is never throttled" principle: exits are unlimited *within* a chain, but the cross-chain return path is rate-limited like any other bridge operation, because a bridge is itself an exposure rather than a retreat.

The generalizable design rule is that a Sky Agent's risk budget is not uniform across its footprint — it contracts with distance from the chain where governance, contracts and enforcement actually live.
description: Solana reserves and bridge-backs cap at 25M with a 10M/day slope while comparable Ethereum limits run 100M with 50M/day, and the asymmetry holds in both bridging directions.
